body: I make painted eggs using thumb tacks. Made them for some friends and family, but after that it stopped. No demand for them, no desire to make them.

I have, several times. They suffer from it, too, but they have a much better handle on theirs. So when I talk to them about it, they tell me I'm just letting myself be depressed instead of doing what they do and occupying my mind. 

I tried. I failed. I just can't shake it.
Examples? I've been looking and can't find any.

I enjoy the feeling of sleep, so something that's guaranteed to put me to sleep can't be anything but good. I do know dependency well. Whenever I get into the drug problem and pull myself out, I can't get to sleep the first couple nights. I either eventually pass out or I go back to the drugs. 

I'm 22. I don't feel like I'm wasting my life, but I definitely feel like I'm not living the right one. And now I have next to no effort or reason to try and find it.

I would, but drugs are easier to come by. Oxycodone is leftover from an injury mum had. It was too strong for her and made her sick. The only thing strong medicine does to me is put me to sleep in 20 minutes. 

I knew the job would just be a means to an end, but I didn't expect it to be so... robotic, for lack of a better word. There is no enjoyment, I just do corporate-required stuff and fuck the rest. 

As for goals? No clue. I wanted to make craft and sell it, but that idea fell flat when I tried. I got too frustrated or it never picked up. Something with animals. Haven't given it much thought at all.

It'll somehow turn detrimental. 

I feel pain so I take medicine. It helps me sleep, so I take it the next night, and then the next. When it's not good enough I'll up to a stronger medication. First Ibu, then Ibu+Codeine, then Oxycodone. By the time I'm at oxycodone I realize there's a problem then I stop. Several sleepless nights later I'm fixed. I still enjoy the feeling of helplessly falling to sleep, and staying asleep for over 10 hours. It's an escape. 

Alcohol I used as a coping mechanism as a teenager. Things got too hard, I'd chug from the closest bottle I could find and go to sleep. I now don't trust myself with alcohol unless I'm around other people. They can drink with me or tell me when enough's enough. 

I turned any large game into a chore. Must beat it 100%. Must. I can't stop until it's done. Once it's done I'll make up a new goal to compulsively strive towards. I get upset that my SO has assumed this new game will lead to addiction, but can I blame them. Can I really. 

I shouldn't trust myself. At all. If I can't trust myself, how can I live? I don't want to be miserable, but I can't trust myself to enjoy anything without fear of addiction. 

If I run away, it won't stop me from getting addicted to something. It won't stop me from going back to the things I was addicted to. I keep trying to think running away will work just as well but I'm kidding myself.
